verses.1:1: The beginning of the Gospel of Jesus Christ, Son of God.
verses.1:2: Just as it is written in the prophet Isaiah: "Look, I am sending My messenger before Your face, who will prepare Your way before You.
verses.1:3: A voice of one calling out in the desert: 'Prepare the way of the Lord; make straight His paths.'"
verses.1:4: John was in the desert baptizing and preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
verses.1:5: And the whole region of Judea and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem were going out to him, and they were being baptized by him in the river Jordan, confessing their sins.
verses.1:6: And John was dressed in camel hair, with a leather belt around his waist, and he ate locusts and wild honey.
verses.1:7: And he was preaching, saying, "One stronger than I is coming after me; I am not worthy to stoop down and untie the strap of His sandals.
verses.1:8: I have baptized you with water, yet He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit."
verses.1:9: And it happened in those days that Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and He was baptized by John in the Jordan.
verses.1:10: And immediately, coming up out of the water, He saw the heavens opened, and the Spirit descending like a dove and remaining in Him.
verses.1:11: And a voice came from the heavens: "You are My beloved Son; in You I am greatly pleased."
verses.1:12: And immediately the Spirit drove Him into the desert.
verses.1:13: And He was in the desert for forty days and forty nights, and was being tempted by Satan; and He was with wild animals, and angels were serving Him.
verses.1:14: Now after John was handed over, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the Gospel of the kingdom of God,
verses.1:15: and saying, "The time has been fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has drawn near; repent and believe the Gospel."
verses.1:16: And passing along beside the Sea of Galilee, He saw Simon and his brother Andrew casting nets into the sea (for they were fishermen),
verses.1:17: and Jesus said to them, "Come after Me, and I will make you become fishers of men."
verses.1:18: And at once, leaving the nets behind, they followed Him.
verses.1:19: And moving on a little way from there, He saw James son of Zebedee and his brother John, who were likewise mending nets in the boat;
verses.1:20: and immediately He called them. And leaving their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired workers, they followed Him.
verses.1:21: And they entered Capernaum; and immediately on the Sabbath, having entered the synagogue, He was teaching them.
verses.1:22: And they were astounded at His teaching, for He was teaching them as one possessing authority, and not like the scribes.
verses.1:23: And in their synagogue there was a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried out,
verses.1:24: saying, "What is there between us and You, Jesus the Nazarene? Have You come to destroy us? I know who You are, the Holy One of God."
verses.1:25: And Jesus sternly rebuked it, saying, "Be silent, and come out of the man."
verses.1:26: And convulsing him and crying out in a loud voice, the unclean spirit went out from him.
verses.1:27: And everyone was amazed, so that they questioned one another, saying, "What is this? What new teaching is this? For with authority He commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey Him."
verses.1:28: And immediately the report about Him went out into the whole region of Galilee.
verses.1:29: And at once, going out from the synagogue, they came into the house of Simon and Andrew with James and John.
verses.1:30: Now Simon's mother-in-law was lying down with a fever, and immediately they spoke to Him about her.
verses.1:31: And approaching, He raised her up, taking hold of her hand; and instantly the fever left her, and she was serving them.
verses.1:32: Now when evening came, after the sun had set, they were bringing to Him all who were unwell and those who had demons;
verses.1:33: and the entire city was assembled at the door.
verses.1:34: And He healed many who were afflicted with various illnesses, and He was casting out many demons; and He would not allow them to speak, because they knew Him.
verses.1:35: And rising very early at dawn, He went out and departed to a deserted place, and there He was praying.
verses.1:36: And Simon and those who were with him went after Him.
verses.1:37: And when they had found Him, they said to Him, "Everyone is looking for You."
verses.1:38: And He said to them, "Let us go into the nearby villages and cities, so that I may preach there as well; for I came for this purpose."
verses.1:39: And He was preaching in their synagogues and in all of Galilee, and casting out demons.
verses.1:40: And a leper came to Him, pleading with Him; and kneeling down, he said to Him, "If You are willing, You are able to cleanse me."
verses.1:41: Now Jesus, having compassion on him, reached out His hand, and touching him, He said to him, "I am willing. Be cleansed."
verses.1:42: And when He had spoken, immediately the leprosy departed from him, and he was cleansed.
verses.1:43: And He sternly warned him and immediately sent him out,
verses.1:44: and said to him, "See that you tell no one; but go, show yourself to the chief priest, and offer for your cleansing the things that Moses commanded, as a testimony to them."
verses.1:45: Yet having gone out, he began to proclaim and spread the word widely, so that He could no longer openly enter a city, but stayed outside in deserted places; and people were gathering to Him from everywhere.
verses.2:1: And He entered Capernaum again after some days,
verses.2:2: and it was heard that He was in the house, and many gathered together, so that there was no room, not even at the door, and He was speaking the word to them.
verses.2:3: And they came to Him, bringing a paralyzed man who was being carried by four.
verses.2:4: And when they could not present him to Him because of the crowd, they uncovered the roof where He was; and making an opening, they lowered the cot on which the paralyzed man was lying.
verses.2:5: Now when Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralyzed man, "Son, your sins are forgiven you."
verses.2:6: Now some of the scribes were sitting there, thinking in their hearts:
verses.2:7: "Why does this man speak like this? He is blaspheming. Who can forgive sins except God alone?"
verses.2:8: Immediately knowing in His spirit that they were thinking this way within themselves, Jesus said to them, "Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?
verses.2:9: Which is easier, to say to the paralyzed man, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Get up, take your cot, and walk'?
verses.2:10: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins" (He said to the paralyzed man),
verses.2:11: "I tell you, get up, take your cot, and go to your house."
verses.2:12: And immediately he got up, and taking up the cot, he went away in front of everyone, so that all were amazed and honored God, saying, "We have never seen anything like this."
verses.2:13: And He went out again to the sea, and all the crowd was coming to Him, and He was teaching them.
verses.2:14: And as He was passing by, He saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth, and He said to him, "Follow Me." And getting up, he followed Him.
verses.2:15: And it happened, as He was reclining at table in his house, that many tax collectors and sinners were reclining together with Jesus and His disciples; for there were many who were also following Him.
verses.2:16: And the scribes and the Pharisees, seeing that He was eating with tax collectors and sinners, were saying to His disciples, "Why does your Teacher eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?"
verses.2:17: Hearing this, Jesus said to them, "The healthy do not need a physician, but those who are unwell; for I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners."
verses.2:18: And the disciples of John and the Pharisees were fasting; and they came and said to Him, "Why do the disciples of John and of the Pharisees fast, but Your disciples do not fast?"
verses.2:19: And Jesus said to them, "Can the sons of the wedding fast as long as the bridegroom is with them? For as long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.
verses.2:20: But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then they will fast in those days.
verses.2:21: No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth onto an old garment; otherwise the new piece pulls away from the old, and a greater tear results.
verses.2:22: And no one puts new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the wine will burst the wineskins, and the wine will be poured out, and the wineskins will be ruined; but new wine must be put into new wineskins."
verses.2:23: And it happened again that the Lord was walking through the grainfields on the Sabbath, and His disciples began to go forward and pluck heads of grain.
verses.2:24: Now the Pharisees were saying to Him, "Look, why are they doing on the Sabbath what is not lawful?"
verses.2:25: And He said to them, "Have you never read what David did when he had need and was hungry, he himself and those who were with him,
verses.2:26: how he entered the house of God under Abiathar the high priest, and ate the loaves of presentation, which it was not lawful to eat except for the priests, and gave them to those who were with him?"
verses.2:27: And He was saying to them, "The Sabbath was made for the sake of man, and not man for the sake of the Sabbath.
verses.2:28: Therefore the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath."
verses.3:1: And He entered the synagogue again, and a man with a withered hand was there.
verses.3:2: And they were watching Him closely to see whether He would heal on the Sabbath, so that they might accuse Him.
verses.3:3: And He said to the man with the withered hand, "Stand up in the middle."
verses.3:4: And He said to them, "Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to destroy it?" But they kept silent.
verses.3:5: And looking around at them with anger, grieved over the blindness of their heart, He said to the man, "Stretch out your hand." And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored to him.
verses.3:6: And going out, the Pharisees immediately began taking counsel with the Herodians against Him, as to how they might destroy Him.
verses.3:7: Now Jesus withdrew with His disciples to the sea, and a large crowd from Galilee and Judea followed Him,
verses.3:8: and from Jerusalem, and from Idumea, and beyond the Jordan; and those around Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, hearing what He was doing, came to Him.
verses.3:9: And He told His disciples that a small boat should be kept ready for Him because of the crowd, so that they would not crush Him;
verses.3:10: for He was healing many, so that all who had afflictions were pressing in upon Him in order to touch Him.
verses.3:11: And whenever the unclean spirits saw Him, they would fall down before Him and cry out, saying,
verses.3:12: "You are the Son of God." And He strictly warned them not to make Him known.
verses.3:13: And going up onto the mountain, He called to Himself those whom He Himself wanted, and they came to Him.
verses.3:14: And He appointed twelve so that they would be with Him, and so that He might send them to preach.
verses.3:15: And He gave them authority to heal illnesses and to drive out demons.
verses.3:16: And He gave Simon the name Peter;
verses.3:17: and James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James, and He gave them the name Boanerges, which is, Sons of Thunder;
verses.3:18: and Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Cananaean,
verses.3:19: and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed Him.
verses.3:20: And they came to a house, and the crowd gathered again, so that they could not even eat bread.
verses.3:21: And when His own people heard this, they went out to take hold of Him; for they were saying, "He has gone mad."
verses.3:22: And the scribes who had come down from Jerusalem were saying, "He has Beelzebub," and, "By the prince of demons He drives out demons."
verses.3:23: And having called them together, He was speaking to them in parables: "How can Satan drive out Satan?
verses.3:24: And if a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
verses.3:25: And if a house is divided against itself, that house cannot stand.
verses.3:26: And if Satan has risen up against himself, he is divided, and he will not be able to stand, but has an end.
verses.3:27: No one can enter the house of a strong man and plunder his belongings unless he first binds the strong man, and then he will plunder his house.
verses.3:28: Amen, I tell you, all sins will be forgiven the sons of men, and the blasphemies with which they blaspheme;
verses.3:29: but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will never have forgiveness, but will be guilty of an eternal offense."
verses.3:30: Because they were saying, "He has an unclean spirit."
verses.3:31: And His mother and brothers came, and standing outside, they sent to Him, calling Him,
verses.3:32: and a crowd was sitting around Him; and they said to Him, "Look, Your mother and Your brothers are outside seeking You."
verses.3:33: And answering them, He said, "Who are My mother and My brothers?"
verses.3:34: And looking around at those who were sitting in a circle around Him, He said, "Here are My mother and My brothers.
verses.3:35: For whoever does the will of God, this one is My brother, and My sister, and mother."
verses.4:1: And again He began to teach by the sea, and a large crowd gathered to Him, so that boarding a boat He sat on the sea, and the entire crowd was along the sea on the land.
verses.4:2: And He was teaching them many things in parables, and He said to them in His teaching:
verses.4:3: "Listen! Look, the sower went out to sow.
verses.4:4: And while he was sowing, some fell along the road, and the birds of the sky came and ate it.
verses.4:5: Yet some fell on rocky places, where it did not have much soil, and immediately it sprang up, because it did not have depth of soil.
verses.4:6: And when the sun rose, it was scorched, and because it did not have a root, it dried up.
verses.4:7: And some fell among thorns, and the thorns came up and choked it, and it produced no fruit.
verses.4:8: And some fell into good soil, and produced fruit rising up and growing, and brought forth, one thirty, one sixty, and one a hundred."
verses.4:9: And He said, "The one who has ears for hearing, let him hear."
verses.4:10: And when He was alone, those who were with Him, the twelve, asked Him about the parable.
verses.4:11: And He said to them, "To you it has been given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God; but to those who are outside, all things happen in parables,
verses.4:12: so that seeing they may see and not see, and hearing they may hear and not understand, that they may never turn and sins be forgiven them."
verses.4:13: And He said to them, "Do you not know this parable? And how will you understand all the parables?
verses.4:14: The one who sows, sows the word.
verses.4:15: Now these are the ones along the road, where the word is sown; and when they have heard, Satan comes at once and takes away the word that has been sown in their hearts.
verses.4:16: And similarly, these are the ones who are sown on rocky places: when they have heard the word, they immediately receive it with joy,
verses.4:17: and they do not have a root in themselves, but are temporary; then, when tribulation and persecution arise on account of the word, at once they stumble.
verses.4:18: And others are those who are sown among thorns; these are the ones who hear the word,
verses.4:19: and the troubles of the age, and the deception of riches, and desires concerning other things entering in choke the word, and it becomes without fruit.
verses.4:20: And these are the ones who were sown on good soil, who hear the word and welcome it and bear fruit, one thirty, one sixty, and one a hundred."
verses.4:21: And He said to them, "Does a lamp come to be placed under a grain measure or under a bed? Is it not to be placed on a lampstand?
verses.4:22: For there is nothing hidden that will not be revealed, nor has anything been made secret except that it may come into the open.
verses.4:23: If anyone has ears for hearing, let him hear."
verses.4:24: And He said to them, "Watch what you hear. With whatever measure you measure, it will be measured back to you, and more will be added to you.
verses.4:25: For it will be given to the one who has, and even what he has will be taken away from the one who does not have."
verses.4:26: And He was saying, "This is how the kingdom of God is: just as if a man should cast seed onto the earth,
verses.4:27: and sleep and rise night and day, and the seed should sprout and grow while he does not know.
verses.4:28: For of its own accord the earth bears fruit: first the blade, then the head, then the full grain in the head.
verses.4:29: And when it has brought forth the fruits, immediately he sends in the sickle, because the harvest is here."
verses.4:30: And He was saying, "To what should we liken the kingdom of God? Or to what parable should we compare it?
verses.4:31: Like a mustard seed, which, when it has been sown in the earth, is smaller than all the seeds that are on the earth;
verses.4:32: and when it has been sown, it comes up and becomes greater than all garden plants, and makes large branches, so that the birds of the sky can dwell under its shade."
verses.4:33: And He was speaking the word to them with many such parables, to the extent that they could hear.
verses.4:34: And without a parable He was not speaking to them, but in private He was explaining all things to His disciples.
verses.4:35: And He said to them on that day, when evening had come, "Let us cross over to the opposite side."
verses.4:36: And dismissing the crowd, they took Him just as He was in the boat, and other boats were with Him.
verses.4:37: And a great storm of wind arose, and it was throwing the waves into the boat, so that the boat was filling up.
verses.4:38: And He Himself was in the stern, sleeping on a pillow; and they woke Him and said to Him, "Teacher, does it not matter to You that we are perishing?"
verses.4:39: And rising up, He rebuked the wind and said to the sea, "Be silent, be mute." And the wind ceased, and a great calm came about.
verses.4:41: And He said to them, "Why are you fearful? Do you not yet have faith?" And they feared with a great fear, and were saying to one another, "Who, do you think, is this, that both the wind and the sea obey Him?"
verses.5:1: And they came across the strait of the sea into the region of the Gerasenes.
verses.5:2: And as He came out of the boat, immediately a man with an unclean spirit met Him out of the tombs,
verses.5:3: who had his dwelling in the tombs, and not even with chains could anyone bind him any longer;
verses.5:4: because, having often been bound with shackles and chains, he had torn the chains apart and shattered the shackles, and no one was able to tame him;
verses.5:5: and always, day and night, he was in the tombs and in the mountains, crying out and cutting himself with stones.
verses.5:6: Now seeing Jesus from a distance, he ran and worshiped Him.
verses.5:7: And crying out with a loud voice, he said, "What is there between me and You, Jesus, Son of God Most High? I adjure You by God not to torture me."
verses.5:8: For He was saying to him, "Come out, unclean spirit, from the man."
verses.5:9: And He asked him, "What is your name?" And he said to Him, "Legion is my name, because we are many."
verses.5:10: And he pleaded with Him earnestly not to drive him outside the region.
verses.5:11: Now a large herd of pigs was feeding there near the mountain.
verses.5:12: And the spirits pleaded with Him, saying, "Send us into the pigs, so that we may enter into them."
verses.5:13: And Jesus immediately granted it to them. And coming out, the unclean spirits entered into the pigs; and with a great rush the herd plunged headlong into the sea, about two thousand, and they were drowned in the sea.
verses.5:14: Now those who were tending them fled and reported it in the city and in the fields. And they went out to see what had happened.
verses.5:15: And they came to Jesus, and saw the one who had been tormented by the demon sitting, clothed, and of sound mind; and they were afraid.
verses.5:16: And those who had seen it recounted to them how it had happened to the one who had had the demon, and about the pigs.
verses.5:17: And they began to ask Him to depart from their territory.
verses.5:18: And as He was getting into the boat, the one who had been tormented by the demon began to plead with Him that he might be with Him.
verses.5:19: And He did not permit him, but said to him, "Go to your house, to your own people, and announce to them how much the Lord has done for you, and how He has had mercy on you."
verses.5:20: And he went away and began to proclaim in the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him; and all were amazed.
verses.5:21: And when Jesus had crossed over again in the boat across the strait, a large crowd gathered to Him, and He was near the sea.
verses.5:22: And one of the synagogue leaders, named Jairus, came, and seeing Him, he fell down at His feet.
verses.5:23: And he pleaded with Him earnestly, saying, "My daughter is at the point of death; come, lay Your hand on her, so that she may be saved and live."
verses.5:24: And He went with him, and a large crowd was following Him, and they were pressing against Him.
verses.5:25: And a woman who had had a flow of blood for twelve years,
verses.5:26: and had endured many things from numerous physicians, and had spent all that was hers, and had gained nothing, but rather was getting worse,
verses.5:27: having heard about Jesus, came from behind in the crowd and touched His garment.
verses.5:28: For she was saying, "If I touch even His garment, I will be saved."
verses.5:29: And at once the source of her blood dried up, and she felt in her body that she had been healed from the affliction.
verses.5:30: And immediately Jesus, perceiving in Himself the power that had gone out from Him, turned to the crowd and said, "Who touched My garments?"
verses.5:31: And His disciples said to Him, "You see the crowd pressing against You, and You say, 'Who touched Me?'"
verses.5:32: And He was looking around to see her who had done this.
verses.5:33: But the woman, fearing and trembling, knowing what had happened in her, came and fell down before Him, and told Him the whole truth.
verses.5:34: But He said to her, "Daughter, your faith has saved you; go in peace, and be healed from your affliction."
verses.5:35: While He was still speaking, some came from the synagogue leader's house, saying, "Your daughter is dead; why do you trouble the Teacher any further?"
verses.5:36: But Jesus, having heard the word that was being spoken, said to the synagogue leader, "Do not be afraid; only believe."
verses.5:37: And He did not permit anyone to follow Him except Peter, and James, and John the brother of James.
verses.5:38: And they came to the house of the synagogue leader, and He saw a commotion, and people weeping and wailing loudly.
verses.5:39: And entering, He said to them, "Why are you in turmoil and weeping? The girl is not dead, but is sleeping."
verses.5:40: And they were laughing at Him. But He, having put everyone out, took the father and the mother of the girl, and those who were with Him, and entered where the girl was lying.
verses.5:41: And holding the girl's hand, He said to her, "Talitha cumi," which is translated, "Girl, I say to you, rise."
verses.5:42: And at once the girl rose and began walking; now she was twelve years old. And they were stunned with great amazement.
verses.5:43: And He strictly commanded them that no one should know this, and He said that something should be given to her to eat.
verses.6:1: And departing from there, He went to His native place, and His disciples were following Him.
verses.6:2: And when the Sabbath came, He began to teach in the synagogue; and many who heard were astonished at His teaching, saying, "Where does this man get all these things? And what is the wisdom that has been given to Him, and such deeds of power that are performed through His hands?
verses.6:3: Is this not the craftsman, the son of Mary, the brother of James, and Joseph, and Judas, and Simon? Are not His sisters also here with us?" And they were taking offense at Him.
verses.6:4: And Jesus said to them, "A prophet is not without honor except in his native place, and in his house, and among his relatives."
verses.6:5: And He could not perform any deed of power there, except that He healed a few sick people by laying His hands on them.
verses.6:6: And He marveled because of their unbelief, and He was going around the surrounding villages, teaching.
verses.6:7: And He called the Twelve, and began to send them out two by two, and He was giving them authority over unclean spirits.
verses.6:8: And He commanded them to take nothing on the way except a staff only: no bag, no bread, and no copper money in their belt,
verses.6:9: but to wear sandals, and not to put on two tunics.
verses.6:10: And He said to them, "Wherever you enter a house, remain there until you depart from there.
verses.6:11: And whoever does not receive you or listen to you, as you go out from there, shake off the dust from your feet as a testimony to them."
verses.6:12: And going out, they preached that people should repent.
verses.6:13: And they were casting out many demons, and anointing many sick people with oil, and healing them.
verses.6:14: And King Herod heard (for His name had become well known), and he was saying, "John the Baptist has risen from the dead, and for this reason powers are at work in him."
verses.6:15: Others, however, were saying, "He is Elijah"; while others were saying, "He is a prophet, like one of the prophets."
verses.6:16: When he heard this, Herod said, "John, whom I beheaded, he has risen from the dead."
verses.6:17: For Herod himself had sent and seized John, and bound him in prison on account of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, because he had married her.
verses.6:18: For John had been saying to Herod, "It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife."
verses.6:19: Now Herodias was plotting against him and wanted to kill him, and could not.
verses.6:20: For Herod feared John, knowing him to be a righteous and holy man, and he kept him safe; and when he heard him, he did many things, and listened to him gladly.
verses.6:21: And when an opportune day arrived, Herod gave a birthday banquet for the nobles, and the tribunes, and the leading men of Galilee.
verses.6:22: And when the daughter of Herodias herself had come in and danced and pleased Herod and those reclining with him, the king said to the girl, "Ask me for what you wish, and I will give it to you."
verses.6:23: And he swore to her, "Whatever you ask, I will give to you, even half of my kingdom."
verses.6:24: And when she had gone out, she said to her mother, "What should I ask for?" And she said, "The head of John the Baptist."
verses.6:25: And when she had come in immediately with haste to the king, she made her request, saying, "I want you to give me at once on a platter the head of John the Baptist."
verses.6:26: And the king was grieved; because of the oath and because of those reclining with him, he did not want to grieve her,
verses.6:27: but having sent an executioner, he commanded his head to be brought on a platter. And he beheaded him in the prison,
verses.6:28: and brought his head on a platter, and gave it to the girl, and the girl gave it to her mother.
verses.6:29: When they heard this, his disciples came and took his body, and placed it in a tomb.
verses.6:30: And gathering together to Jesus, the apostles reported to Him everything that they had done and had taught.
verses.6:31: And He said to them, "Come away by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a little." For there were many who were coming and going, and they did not even have time to eat.
verses.6:32: And boarding a boat, they went away to a deserted place by themselves.
verses.6:33: And people saw them departing, and many recognized them; and on foot from all the cities they ran together there and arrived ahead of them.
verses.6:34: And coming out, Jesus saw a large crowd, and He had compassion on them, because they were like sheep not having a shepherd; and He began to teach many things.
verses.6:35: And when the hour was already late, His disciples approached, saying, "This place is deserted, and the hour has already passed;
verses.6:36: send them away, so that going into the nearest hamlets and villages, they may buy themselves food to eat."
verses.6:37: And answering, He said to them, "You give them something to eat." And they said to Him, "Should we go and buy loaves for two hundred denarii and give them something to eat?"
verses.6:38: And He said to them, "How many loaves do you have? Go and see." And when they had found out, they said, "Five, and two fish."
verses.6:39: And He commanded them to have everyone recline in companies on the green grass.
verses.6:40: And they reclined in groups, by hundreds and by fifties.
verses.6:41: And having taken the five loaves and the two fish, looking up to heaven, He blessed and broke the loaves, and gave them to His disciples to set before them; and He divided the two fish among them all.
verses.6:42: And they all ate and were satisfied.
verses.6:43: And they picked up the leftovers, twelve baskets full of fragments, and of the fish.
verses.6:44: Now those who ate were five thousand men.
verses.6:45: And immediately He compelled His disciples to board the boat, so that they would go ahead of Him across the water to Bethsaida, while He Himself dismissed the people.
verses.6:46: And when He had dismissed them, He went away to the mountain to pray.
verses.6:47: And when evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and He Himself was alone on the land.
verses.6:48: And He saw them straining at rowing (for the wind was against them), and around the fourth watch of the night He came to them, walking on the sea; and He wanted to pass by them.
verses.6:49: But when they saw Him walking on the sea, they thought it was a ghost, and they cried out.
verses.6:50: For they all saw Him and were deeply troubled. And immediately He spoke with them and said to them, "Have courage, it is I; do not be afraid."
verses.6:51: And He climbed into the boat with them, and the wind ceased. And they were all the more astonished within themselves.
verses.6:52: For they had not understood about the loaves, for their heart was blinded.
verses.6:53: And when they had crossed over, they came to the land of Gennesaret and landed.
verses.6:54: And when they had come out of the boat, people immediately recognized Him,
verses.6:55: and running through that entire region, they began to carry around on mats those who were ill, wherever they heard He was.
verses.6:56: And wherever He entered, into villages, or into hamlets, or cities, they would place the sick in the public squares and beg Him that they might touch even the fringe of His garment; and as many as touched Him were made well.
verses.7:1: And the Pharisees and some of the scribes, coming from Jerusalem, gathered to Him.
verses.7:2: And when they saw some of His disciples eating bread with common hands, that is, unwashed, they found fault.
verses.7:3: For the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands frequently, holding to the tradition of the elders;
verses.7:4: and coming from the marketplace, they do not eat unless they wash themselves; and there are many other things that have been handed down to them to keep: washings of cups, and pitchers, and bronze vessels, and couches.
verses.7:5: And the Pharisees and the scribes asked Him, "Why do Your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with common hands?"
verses.7:6: But answering, He said to them, "Isaiah prophesied well about you hypocrites, as it is written: 'This people honors Me with their lips, but their heart is far from Me;
verses.7:7: and in vain they worship Me, teaching doctrines and precepts of men.'
verses.7:8: For abandoning the commandment of God, you hold to the tradition of men, washings of pitchers and cups; and you do many other things like these."
verses.7:9: And He was saying to them, "How well you nullify the precept of God, so that you may keep your tradition!
verses.7:10: For Moses said, 'Honor your father and your mother,' and, 'Whoever curses father or mother, let him surely die.'
verses.7:11: But you say, 'If a man says to father or mother, Corban (which is a gift) is whatever from me would benefit you,'
verses.7:12: and you no longer allow him to do anything for his father or mother,
verses.7:13: invalidating the word of God through your tradition that you have handed down; and you do many similar things of this kind."
verses.7:14: And calling the crowd again, He was saying to them, "Listen to Me, all of you, and understand.
verses.7:15: There is nothing outside a man, entering into him, that can pollute him; but the things that proceed from a man, those are what defile a man."
verses.7:17: And when He had entered the house away from the crowd, His disciples were asking Him about the parable.
verses.7:18: And He said to them, "Are you also so lacking in understanding? Do you not understand that everything entering into a man from outside cannot defile him,
verses.7:19: because it does not enter into his heart, but goes into the stomach and goes out into the latrine, cleansing all foods?"
verses.7:20: And He was saying, "The things that go out of a man, those defile a man.
verses.7:21: For from within, out of the heart of men, evil thoughts proceed: adulteries, fornications, murders,
verses.7:22: thefts, greed, wickedness, deceit, lewdness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness.
verses.7:23: All these evils proceed from within, and they defile a man."
verses.7:24: And rising from there, He went away into the territory of Tyre and Sidon; and entering a house, He wanted no one to know, and He could not remain hidden.
verses.7:25: For a woman whose daughter had an unclean spirit, as soon as she heard about Him, entered and fell down at His feet.
verses.7:26: For the woman was a Gentile, a Syrophoenician by birth. And she kept asking Him to cast the demon out of her daughter.
verses.7:27: And He said to her, "Allow the children to be satisfied first; for it is not good to take the bread of the children and throw it to the dogs."
verses.7:28: But she answered and said to Him, "Yes, Lord; for even the little dogs eat under the table from the crumbs of the children."
verses.7:29: And He said to her, "On account of this statement, go; the demon has gone out from your daughter."
verses.7:30: And when she had gone away to her house, she found the girl lying on the bed, and that the demon had gone out.
verses.7:31: And going out again from the territory of Tyre, He came through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee, through the middle of the territory of the Decapolis.
verses.7:32: And they brought to Him a deaf and mute man, and they were imploring Him to lay His hand on him.
verses.7:33: And taking him aside from the crowd, He put His fingers into his ears; and spitting, He touched his tongue.
verses.7:34: And looking up to heaven, He sighed deeply and said to him, "Ephphatha," which is, "Be opened."
verses.7:35: And immediately his ears were opened, and the bond of his tongue was released, and he was speaking properly.
verses.7:36: And He commanded them not to tell anyone; yet the more He kept commanding them, so much the more abundantly they kept proclaiming it,
verses.7:37: and even more they marveled, saying, "He has done everything well; He has made both the deaf hear and the mute speak."
verses.8:1: In those days, when a large crowd was there again and they did not have anything to eat, having called the disciples together, He said to them,
verses.8:2: "I have compassion on the crowd, because, look, they have already stayed with Me for three days and do not have anything to eat;
verses.8:3: and if I send them away fasting to their home, they will grow faint on the way, for some of them have come from a distance."
verses.8:4: And His disciples answered Him, "From where will anyone be able to satisfy them with bread in the wilderness?"
verses.8:5: And He asked them, "How many loaves do you have?" And they said, "Seven."
verses.8:6: And He instructed the crowd to recline on the ground. And taking the seven loaves, giving thanks, He broke them and kept giving them to His disciples to serve, and they served them to the crowd.
verses.8:7: And they had a few small fish; and He blessed these as well and ordered them to be served.
verses.8:8: And they ate and were satisfied; and they picked up what was left over of the broken pieces, seven large baskets.
verses.8:9: Now those who ate were about four thousand, and He sent them away.
verses.8:10: And immediately, boarding the boat with His disciples, He came into the region of Dalmanutha.
verses.8:11: And the Pharisees came out and began to dispute with Him, seeking from Him a sign from heaven, testing Him.
verses.8:12: And groaning in spirit, He said, "Why is this generation seeking a sign? Amen, I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation."
verses.8:13: And leaving them, He boarded the boat again and departed across the sea.
verses.8:14: And they forgot to take bread, and except for one loaf they had none with them in the boat.
verses.8:15: And He was instructing them, saying, "Watch out and guard against the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod."
verses.8:16: And they were reasoning with one another, saying, "Because we have no bread."
verses.8:17: Perceiving this, Jesus said to them, "Why are you reasoning because you have no bread? Will you not yet perceive, nor do you understand? Do you still have your heart blinded?
verses.8:18: Having eyes, do you not see? And having ears, do you not hear? Nor do you recall,
verses.8:19: when I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces did you pick up?" They said to Him, "Twelve."
verses.8:20: "When I also broke the seven loaves for the four thousand, how many large baskets of broken pieces did you pick up?" And they said to Him, "Seven."
verses.8:21: And He was saying to them, "How is it that you do not yet understand?"
verses.8:22: And they came to Bethsaida, and they brought a blind man to Him, and were pleading with Him to touch him.
verses.8:23: And taking hold of the blind man's hand, He led him outside the village; and spitting on his eyes, having laid His hands on him, He asked him if he saw anything.
verses.8:24: And looking, he said, "I see men like trees walking."
verses.8:25: Then He laid His hands on his eyes again, and he began to see, and he was restored so that he saw all things clearly.
verses.8:26: And He sent him to his home, saying, "Go to your home, and if you enter the village, tell no one."
verses.8:27: And Jesus and His disciples went out into the towns of Caesarea Philippi; and on the way He was asking His disciples, saying to them, "Who do men say that I am?"
verses.8:28: They answered Him, saying, "John the Baptist; others, Elijah; and others, as one of the prophets."
verses.8:29: Then He said to them, "But you, who do you say that I am?" Peter, answering, said to Him, "You are the Christ."
verses.8:30: And He sternly warned them not to tell anyone about Him.
verses.8:31: And He began to teach them that it is necessary for the Son of Man to suffer many things, and to be rejected by the elders and by the chief priests and the scribes, and to be put to death, and after three days to rise again.
verses.8:32: And He was speaking the word openly. And taking hold of Him, Peter began to rebuke Him.
verses.8:33: But He, turning around and seeing His disciples, sternly rebuked Peter, saying, "Go behind Me, Satan, because you do not have a mind for the things of God, but for the things of men."
verses.8:34: And having called the crowd together with His disciples, He said to them, "If anyone wants to follow Me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow Me.
verses.8:35: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life on account of Me and the Gospel will save it.
verses.8:36: For what will it profit a man if he gains the entire world and incurs the loss of his soul?
verses.8:37: Or what will a man give in exchange for his soul?
verses.8:38: For the one who is ashamed of Me and of My words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when He comes in His Father's glory with the holy angels."
verses.9:1: And He was saying to them, "Amen, I tell you that there are some of those standing here who will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God coming in power."
verses.9:2: And after six days, Jesus took along Peter and James and John, and led them onto a high mountain apart by themselves, and He was transfigured before them.
verses.9:3: And His garments became gleaming and exceedingly white like snow, such as a launderer on earth cannot make white.
verses.9:4: And Elijah appeared to them with Moses, and they were speaking with Jesus.
verses.9:5: And Peter, answering, said to Jesus, "Rabbi, it is good for us to be here; and let us make three tents, one for You, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah."
verses.9:6: For he did not know what he should say, for they were terrified with fear.
verses.9:7: And a cloud formed, overshadowing them, and a voice came out of the cloud, saying, "This is My most beloved Son; listen to Him."
verses.9:8: And immediately, looking around, they no longer saw anyone except Jesus alone with them.
verses.9:9: And as they were coming down from the mountain, He commanded them not to recount to anyone the things they had seen, except when the Son of Man has risen from the dead.
verses.9:10: And they kept the saying to themselves, debating what "when He has risen from the dead" meant.
verses.9:11: And they were asking Him, saying, "Why then do the Pharisees and scribes say that Elijah must come first?"
verses.9:12: And He, answering, said to them, "Elijah, when he comes first, will restore all things; and how is it written concerning the Son of Man that He should suffer many things and be despised?
verses.9:13: But I tell you that Elijah has indeed come (and they did to him whatever they wished), just as it is written about him."
verses.9:14: And coming to His disciples, He saw a great crowd around them, and scribes debating with them.
verses.9:15: And immediately all the people, seeing Jesus, were astounded and struck with fear, and running up, they were greeting Him.
verses.9:16: And He asked them, "What are you debating among yourselves?"
verses.9:17: And one from the crowd, answering, said, "Teacher, I have brought to You my son, who has a mute spirit;
verses.9:18: and wherever it seizes him, it dashes him down, and he foams, and grinds his teeth, and wastes away; and I told Your disciples to cast it out, and they could not."
verses.9:19: And He, answering them, said, "Unbelieving generation, how long will I be with you? How long will I bear with you? Bring him to Me."
verses.9:20: And they brought him. And when it saw Him, the spirit immediately convulsed him; and dashed to the ground, he was rolling around, foaming.
verses.9:21: And He asked his father, "How much time has it been since this happened to him?" And he said, "From infancy;
verses.9:22: and frequently it has thrown him into the fire and into the waters to destroy him; but if You can do anything, help us, having compassion on us."
verses.9:23: And Jesus said to him, "If you are able to believe, all things are possible for the one who believes."
verses.9:24: And immediately the father of the boy, crying out, was saying with tears, "I believe, Lord; help my unbelief."
verses.9:25: And when Jesus saw a crowd running together, He rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it, "Deaf and mute spirit, I command you, come out of him, and do not enter into him anymore."
verses.9:26: And crying out and greatly wrenching him, it came out of him, and he became like one dead, so that many were saying, "He is dead."
verses.9:27: But Jesus, taking hold of his hand, lifted him up, and he stood up.
verses.9:28: And when He had entered the house, His disciples were asking Him privately, "Why could we not cast it out?"
verses.9:29: And He said to them, "This kind can come out by nothing except by prayer and fasting."
verses.9:30: And departing from there, they were passing through Galilee, and He did not want anyone to know.
verses.9:31: Now He was teaching His disciples, and He was saying to them, "The Son of Man will be delivered into the hands of men, and they will kill Him; and having been killed, on the third day He will rise."
verses.9:32: But they did not understand the saying, and they were afraid to ask Him.
verses.9:33: And they came to Capernaum. And when they were in the house, He was asking them, "What were you discussing on the way?"
verses.9:34: But they kept silent, for on the way they had disputed among themselves who among them was greater.
verses.9:35: And sitting down, He called the twelve and said to them, "If anyone wants to be first, he will be the last of all and the servant of all."
verses.9:36: And taking a child, He set him in their midst; and when He had embraced him, He said to them,
verses.9:37: "Whoever receives one of such children in My name receives Me; and whoever welcomes Me does not welcome Me, but Him who sent Me."
verses.9:38: John answered Him, saying, "Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in Your name who does not follow us, and we forbade him."
verses.9:39: But Jesus said, "Do not forbid him, for there is no one who performs a mighty work in My name and can quickly speak evil of Me.
verses.9:40: For the one who is not against you is for you.
verses.9:41: For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink in My name, because you belong to Christ, amen, I tell you, he will not lose his reward.
verses.9:42: And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it would be better for him if a donkey's millstone were placed around his neck and he were thrown into the sea.
verses.9:43: And if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off; it is better for you to enter into life maimed than, having two hands, to go into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire.
verses.9:45: And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off; it is better for you to enter into eternal life lame than, having two feet, to be thrown into the Gehenna of unquenchable fire.
verses.9:47: And if your eye causes you to stumble, cast it out; it is better for you to enter into the kingdom of God one-eyed than, having two eyes, to be thrown into the Gehenna of fire,
verses.9:48: where their worm does not die, and the fire is not quenched.
verses.9:49: For everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be salted with salt.
verses.9:50: Salt is good; but if the salt becomes saltless, with what will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and have peace among yourselves."
verses.10:1: And rising up from there, He came into the territory of Judea beyond the Jordan; and crowds gathered to Him again, and as He was accustomed, He was teaching them again.
verses.10:2: And Pharisees approached and were questioning Him whether it is lawful for a man to send away a wife, testing Him.
verses.10:3: But answering, He said to them, "What did Moses command you?"
verses.10:4: They said, "Moses permitted writing a certificate of divorce and sending her away."
verses.10:5: Answering them, Jesus said, "Because of the hardness of your heart, he wrote this commandment for you;
verses.10:6: yet from the beginning of creation, God made them male and female.
verses.10:7: For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and will cling to his wife,
verses.10:8: and the two will be in one flesh. And so they are no longer two, but one flesh.
verses.10:9: Therefore, what God has united, let no human being separate."
verses.10:10: And in the house, His disciples questioned Him again about the same matter.
verses.10:11: And He said to them, "Whoever sends away his wife and marries another commits adultery against her.
verses.10:12: And if a wife sends away her husband and marries another, she commits adultery."
verses.10:13: And they were bringing little children to Him so that He might touch them. But the disciples were rebuking those who were bringing them.
verses.10:14: When Jesus saw them, He was indignant and said to them, "Allow the little children to come to Me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such ones.
verses.10:15: Amen, I tell you: whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will not enter into it."
verses.10:16: And embracing them and laying hands on them, He was blessing them.
verses.10:17: And when He had gone out onto the road, a certain man ran up and, kneeling before Him, was asking Him, "Good Teacher, what should I do so that I may obtain eternal life?"
verses.10:18: But Jesus said to him, "Why do you call Me good? No one is good except the one God.
verses.10:19: You know the commandments: do not commit adultery, do not kill, do not steal, do not give false testimony, do not commit fraud, honor your father and mother."
verses.10:20: But answering, he said to Him, "Teacher, I have observed all these things from my youth."
verses.10:21: And Jesus, looking intently at him, loved him and said to him, "One thing is lacking to you: go, sell whatever you have, and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow Me."
verses.10:22: And saddened at the word, he went away grieving, for he had many possessions.
verses.10:23: And looking around, Jesus said to His disciples, "With what difficulty will those who have riches enter into the kingdom of God!"
verses.10:24: And the disciples were astounded at His words. But Jesus, answering again, said to them, "Little children, how difficult it is for those who trust in riches to enter into the kingdom of God!
verses.10:25: It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a wealthy person to enter into the kingdom of God."
verses.10:26: And they were even more amazed, saying to themselves, "And who can be saved?"
verses.10:27: And looking intently at them, Jesus said, "With human beings it is impossible, but not with God; for all things are possible with God."
verses.10:28: And Peter began to say to Him, "Look, we have left everything and have followed You."
verses.10:29: Answering, Jesus said, "Amen, I tell you: there is no one who has left house, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or children, or fields on account of Me and on account of the Gospel,
verses.10:30: who will not receive a hundred times as much now in this time: houses, and brothers, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and fields, with persecutions, and in the age to come, eternal life.
verses.10:31: Yet many who are first will be last, and the last will be first."
verses.10:32: Now they were on the road going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was going ahead of them, and they were astonished, and those following were afraid. And taking the twelve to Himself again, He began to tell them what things were about to happen to Him:
verses.10:33: "Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests, and to the scribes, and to the elders, and they will condemn Him to death and will hand Him over to the Gentiles;
verses.10:34: and they will mock Him, and spit on Him, and flog Him, and kill Him; and on the third day He will rise again."
verses.10:35: And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came up to Him, saying, "Teacher, we want You to do for us whatever we ask."
verses.10:36: And He said to them, "What do you want Me to do for you?"
verses.10:37: And they said, "Grant us that we may sit, one at Your right hand and the other at Your left hand, in Your glory."
verses.10:38: But Jesus said to them, "You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink, or to be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?"
verses.10:39: And they said to Him, "We are able." And Jesus said to them, "Indeed, the cup that I drink, you will drink; and with the baptism with which I am baptized, you will be baptized;
verses.10:40: but to sit at My right hand or at My left is not Mine to give to you, but it is for those for whom it has been prepared."
verses.10:41: And when the ten heard, they began to be indignant about James and John.
verses.10:42: But Jesus, calling them, said to them, "You know that those who are regarded as ruling over the Gentiles exercise dominion over them, and their rulers hold authority over them.
verses.10:43: Yet it is not this way among you; instead, whoever wishes to become greater will be your servant,
verses.10:44: and whoever wishes to be first among you will be the slave of all.
verses.10:45: For indeed, the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve and to give His life as a redemption for many."
verses.10:46: And they came to Jericho; and as He and His disciples and a very large crowd were departing from Jericho, the son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus, a blind man, was sitting beside the road, begging.
verses.10:47: And when he had heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out and say, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me."
verses.10:48: And many were rebuking him so that he would be silent. But he was crying out all the more, "Son of David, have mercy on me."
verses.10:49: And stopping, Jesus commanded him to be called. And they called the blind man, saying to him, "Take heart; get up, He is calling you."
verses.10:50: Throwing off his cloak and leaping up, he came to Him.
verses.10:51: And answering, Jesus said to him, "What do you want Me to do for you?" And the blind man said to Him, "Rabboni, that I may see."
verses.10:52: And Jesus said to him, "Go, your faith has made you whole." And immediately he saw, and he was following Him on the road.
verses.11:1: And as they were approaching Jerusalem and Bethany, at the Mount of Olives, He sent two of His disciples,
verses.11:2: and said to them, "Go into the village that is opposite you, and immediately upon entering it, you will find a colt tied, on which no person has yet sat. Untie it and bring it.
verses.11:3: And if anyone says to you, 'What are you doing?' say that it is needed by the Lord, and at once he will send it here."
verses.11:4: And going away, they found a colt tied in front of a door, outside where two roads met, and they untied it.
verses.11:5: And some of those standing there were saying to them, "What are you doing, untying the colt?"
verses.11:6: They spoke to them just as Jesus had instructed them, and they permitted them.
verses.11:7: And they led the colt to Jesus, and placed their garments on it, and He sat on it.
verses.11:8: And many spread their garments on the road, while others were cutting leafy branches from the trees and spreading them on the road.
verses.11:9: And those who were going ahead and those who were following were crying out, saying, "Hosanna! Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!
verses.11:10: Blessed is the kingdom of our father David that comes! Hosanna in the highest!"
verses.11:11: And He entered Jerusalem, into the temple; and having looked around at everything, since it was already the evening hour, He went out to Bethany with the twelve.
verses.11:12: And on the following day, as they were going out from Bethany, He became hungry.
verses.11:13: And when He saw from a distance a fig tree having leaves, He went to see if perhaps He might find anything on it; and when He came to it, He found nothing except leaves, for it was not the time for figs.
verses.11:14: And answering, He said to it, "May no one eat fruit from you anymore, forever." And His disciples were listening.
verses.11:15: And they came into Jerusalem. And when He had entered the temple, He began to drive out those selling and buying in the temple, and He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves.
verses.11:16: And He would not allow anyone to carry a vessel through the temple.
verses.11:17: And He was teaching, saying to them, "Is it not written, 'My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations'? But you have made it a cave of robbers."
verses.11:18: When the chief priests and the scribes heard this, they were seeking how they might destroy Him; for they feared Him, because the entire crowd was astonished at His teaching.
verses.11:19: And when evening had come, He went out from the city.
verses.11:20: And as they were passing by in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from the roots.
verses.11:21: And Peter, remembering, said to Him, "Rabbi, look, the fig tree that You cursed has withered!"
verses.11:22: And answering, Jesus said to them, "Have faith in God.
verses.11:23: Amen, I tell you that whoever says to this mountain, 'Be lifted up and be thrown into the sea,' and does not waver in his heart, but believes that whatever he says will happen, it will happen for him.
verses.11:24: Therefore I say to you, all things that you ask for while praying, believe that you will receive them, and they will come about for you.
verses.11:25: And when you stand to pray, forgive, if you hold anything against anyone, so that your Father also, who is in heaven, may forgive you your sins."
verses.11:27: And they came again to Jerusalem. And as He was walking in the temple, the chief priests and the scribes and the elders came to Him,
verses.11:28: and said to Him, "By what authority do You do these things? And who gave You this authority to do these things?"
verses.11:29: But Jesus, answering, said to them, "I also will ask you one question, and answer Me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.
verses.11:30: The baptism of John, was it from heaven or from men? Answer Me."
verses.11:31: But they were reasoning among themselves, saying, "If we say, 'From heaven,' He will say, 'Why then did you not believe him?'
verses.11:32: If we say, 'From men,' we fear the people; for all held that John was truly a prophet."
verses.11:33: And answering, they said to Jesus, "We do not know." And answering, Jesus said to them, "Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things."
verses.12:1: And He began to speak to them in parables: "A man planted a vineyard, and put a hedge around it, and dug a vat, and built a tower, and leased it to farmers, and went abroad.
verses.12:2: And in season he sent a servant to the farmers, so that he might receive from the farmers some of the fruit of the vineyard.
verses.12:3: They seized him, beat him, and sent him away empty-handed.
verses.12:4: And again he sent another servant to them; and they wounded him in the head and treated him with insults.
verses.12:5: And once more he sent another, and they killed him; and many others: some they beat, while others they killed.
verses.12:6: Therefore, still having one dearest son, he sent him also to them last, saying, 'They will respect my son.'
verses.12:7: But the tenants said to one another, 'This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and ours will be the inheritance.'
verses.12:8: And seizing him, they killed him and threw him outside the vineyard.
verses.12:9: What then will the master of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the tenants, and give the vineyard to others.
verses.12:10: Have you not even read this Scripture: 'The stone that the builders rejected, this has become the head of the corner;
verses.12:11: by the Lord this has been done, and it is marvelous in our eyes'?"
verses.12:12: And they were seeking to lay hold of Him, and they feared the crowd; for they realized that He had spoken this parable against them. And leaving Him, they went away.
verses.12:13: And they sent to Him some of the Pharisees and the Herodians, so that they might catch Him in speech.
verses.12:14: And coming, they said to Him, "Teacher, we know that You are truthful and are not concerned about anyone; for You do not look at the face of men, but in truth You teach the way of God. Is it lawful for tribute to be given to Caesar, or shall we not give it?"
verses.12:15: But He, knowing their craftiness, said to them, "Why do you test Me? Bring Me a denarius so that I may see it."
verses.12:16: And they brought one to Him. And He said to them, "Whose is this image and inscription?" They said to Him, "Caesar's."
verses.12:17: And answering, Jesus said to them, "Give back, therefore, the things that are Caesar's to Caesar, and the things that are God's to God." And they were marveling at Him.
verses.12:18: And Sadducees came to Him, who say that there is no resurrection, and they were questioning Him, saying,
verses.12:19: "Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if anyone's brother dies and leaves behind a wife, and leaves no children, his brother should take his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
verses.12:20: There were, then, seven brothers; and the first took a wife, and died leaving no offspring.
verses.12:21: And the second took her and died, and neither did he leave offspring. And the third likewise.
verses.12:22: And the seven took her likewise, and left no offspring. Last of all, the woman also died.
verses.12:23: In the resurrection, therefore, when they rise, whose wife among these will she be? For the seven had her as wife."
verses.12:24: And answering, Jesus said to them, "Are you not in error for this reason, not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of God?
verses.12:25: For when they rise from the dead, they will neither marry nor be married, but are like angels in heaven.
verses.12:26: But concerning the dead, that they rise, have you not read in the book of Moses, at the bush, how God spoke to him, saying, 'I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob'?
verses.12:27: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. You, therefore, are greatly in error."
verses.12:28: And one of the scribes approached, who had heard them disputing, and seeing that He had answered them well, he asked Him which was the first commandment of all.
verses.12:29: And Jesus answered him, "The first commandment of all is: 'Hear, Israel: the Lord your God is one God,
verses.12:30: and you shall love the Lord your God with your entire heart, and with your entire soul, and with your entire mind, and with your entire strength.' This is the first commandment.
verses.12:31: And the second is like it: 'You shall love your neighbor just as yourself.' No other commandment is greater than these."
verses.12:32: And the scribe said to Him, "Rightly, Teacher, You have spoken in truth, that God is one, and there is no other besides Him.
verses.12:33: And for Him to be loved with the entire heart, and with the entire understanding, and with the entire soul, and with the entire strength, and to love one's neighbor just as oneself, is greater than all burnt offerings and sacrifices."
verses.12:34: And Jesus, seeing that he had answered wisely, said to him, "You are not far from the kingdom of God." And no one dared to question Him any longer.
verses.12:35: And answering, Jesus was saying while teaching in the temple, "How do the scribes say that the Christ is the son of David?
verses.12:36: For David himself says in the Holy Spirit: 'The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at My right hand, until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.'
verses.12:37: David himself, therefore, calls Him Lord, and how is He his son?" And a large crowd listened to Him gladly.
verses.12:38: And He was saying to them in His teaching, "Beware of the scribes, who desire to walk in long robes and to be greeted in the marketplace,
verses.12:39: and to sit in the first seats in the synagogues, and the first places at banquets;
verses.12:40: who devour the houses of widows under the pretext of lengthy prayer: these will receive a heavier judgment."
verses.12:41: And Jesus, sitting opposite the treasury, was watching how the crowd was dropping money into the treasury, and many rich people were dropping in much.
verses.12:42: And when one poor widow came, she put in two small coins, which is a quadrans.
verses.12:43: And calling His disciples together, He said to them, "Amen, I tell you that this poor widow has put in more than all who put into the treasury.
verses.12:44: For all of them put in out of what was abundant to them; she, however, out of her poverty put in everything that she had, her entire livelihood."
verses.13:1: And as He was going out of the temple, one of His disciples said to Him, "Teacher, look what stones and what structures!"
verses.13:2: And answering, Jesus said to him, "Do you see all these great buildings? Not a stone will be left upon a stone that will not be torn down."
verses.13:3: And as He was sitting on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew were questioning Him privately:
verses.13:4: "Tell us, when will these things happen? And what will be the sign when all these things begin to be completed?"
verses.13:5: And answering, Jesus began to say to them, "Watch out that nothing misleads you;
verses.13:6: for many will come in My name, saying, 'I am,' and they will mislead many.
verses.13:7: Now when you hear of wars and reports of wars, do not be afraid; for these things must happen, but the end is not yet.
verses.13:8: For nation will rise up against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be earthquakes from place to place, and famines. These are the beginning of pains.
verses.13:9: But watch out for yourselves. For they will hand you over to councils, and in synagogues you will be beaten, and you will stand before governors and kings on account of Me, as a testimony to them.
verses.13:10: And among all nations the gospel must first be proclaimed.
verses.13:11: And when they lead you away, handing you over, do not think beforehand about what you should speak, but whatever is given to you in that hour, speak that; for it is not you who are speaking, but the Holy Spirit.
verses.13:12: And brother will hand over brother to death, and a father his son; and children will rise up against parents and put them to death.
verses.13:13: And you will be hated by everyone on account of My name. But the one who endures to the end, this one will be saved.
verses.13:14: Now when you see the abomination of desolation standing where it should not be (let the one who reads understand), then let those who are in Judea flee into the mountains;
verses.13:15: and let the one who is on the roof not go down into the house, nor enter to take anything out of his house;
verses.13:16: and let the one who will be in the field not turn back to take his garment.
verses.13:17: But woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days.
verses.13:18: And pray that these things may not happen in winter.
verses.13:19: For those days will be tribulations such as have not been from the beginning of creation, which God made, until now, nor will come to be.
verses.13:20: And if the Lord had not shortened the days, no flesh would have been saved; but on account of the chosen ones, whom He chose, He shortened the days.
verses.13:21: And then, if anyone says to you, 'Look, here is the Christ; look, there!' do not believe it.
verses.13:22: For false christs and false prophets will rise up and will give signs and wonders to mislead, if it is possible, even the chosen ones.
verses.13:23: You, therefore, watch out; look, I have told you all things beforehand.
verses.13:24: But in those days, after that tribulation, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its brightness,
verses.13:25: and the stars of heaven will be falling down, and the powers that are in the heavens will be shaken.
verses.13:26: And then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.
verses.13:27: And then He will send His angels and will gather His chosen ones from the four winds, from the farthest point of the earth all the way to the farthest point of heaven.
verses.13:28: Now learn a parable from the fig tree. When its branch has already become tender and leaves have sprouted, you recognize that summer is near;
verses.13:29: so you also, when you see these things happening, know that He is near, at the doors.
verses.13:30: Amen, I tell you that this generation will not pass away until all these things happen.
verses.13:31: Heaven and earth will pass away, yet My words will not pass away.
verses.13:32: But concerning that day or hour no one knows, neither the angels in heaven nor the Son, except the Father.
verses.13:33: Watch out, stay awake, and pray, for you do not know when the time is.
verses.13:34: Just as a man who, having gone on a journey abroad, left his house and gave his servants authority over each task, and commanded the doorkeeper to stay awake,
verses.13:35: stay awake, therefore (for you do not know when the master of the house is coming: in the evening, or at midnight, or at the rooster's crow, or in the morning),
verses.13:36: so that, when he comes suddenly, he may not find you sleeping.
verses.13:37: Now what I say to you, I say to everyone: Stay awake."
verses.14:1: Now the Passover and Unleavened Bread were in two days, and the chief priests and scribes were seeking how they might lay hold of Him by deceit and kill Him.
verses.14:2: But they were saying, "Not on the feast day, for fear that an uproar might arise among the people."
verses.14:3: And while He was in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper and was reclining at table, a woman came holding an alabaster flask of costly spikenard ointment; and having broken the alabaster flask, she poured it over His head.
verses.14:4: However, there were some who were indignant within themselves and saying, "For what purpose has this waste of ointment occurred?
verses.14:5: For this ointment could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and given to the poor." And they were grumbling angrily against her.
verses.14:6: But Jesus said, "Let her be; why are you troubling her? She has performed a good work toward Me.
verses.14:7: For you have the poor with you always, and whenever you wish, you are able to do them good; yet Me you do not always have.
verses.14:8: This woman did what she was able; she came beforehand to anoint My body for burial.
verses.14:9: Amen, I tell you, wherever this Gospel is proclaimed in the entire world, what this woman did will also be recounted in remembrance of her."
verses.14:10: And Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve, went off to the chief priests so that he might betray Him to them.
verses.14:11: Hearing this, they rejoiced and promised that they would give him money. And he kept seeking how he might hand Him over at a favorable moment.
verses.14:12: And on the first day of Unleavened Bread, when they sacrificed the Passover, the disciples said to Him, "Where do You wish us to go and prepare for You so that You may eat the Passover?"
verses.14:13: And He sent two of His disciples and said to them, "Go into the city, and a man carrying a jar of water will meet you; follow him,
verses.14:14: and wherever he enters, say to the master of the house that the Teacher says, 'Where is My dining room, where I may eat the Passover with My disciples?'
verses.14:15: And he himself will show you a large upper room, furnished; and prepare for us there."
verses.14:16: And His disciples went off and came into the city, and they found it just as He had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
verses.14:17: Now when evening had arrived, He came with the Twelve.
verses.14:18: And while they were reclining and eating, Jesus said, "Amen, I tell you that one of you will hand Me over, one who is eating with Me."
verses.14:19: But they began to be saddened and to say to Him one by one, "Surely not I?"
verses.14:20: He said to them, "One of the Twelve, the one who dips his hand with Me in the dish.
verses.14:21: And the Son of Man indeed goes as it is written about Him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man will be handed over! It would have been good for him if that man had not been born."
verses.14:22: And while they were eating, Jesus took bread, and pronouncing a blessing, He broke it and gave it to them, and said, "Take; this is My body."
verses.14:23: And having taken a cup, giving thanks, He gave it to them, and all of them drank from it.
verses.14:24: And He said to them, "This is My blood of the new covenant, which will be poured out for many.
verses.14:25: Amen, I tell you that I will no longer drink from this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God."
verses.14:26: And after a hymn had been recited, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
verses.14:27: And Jesus said to them, "All of you will be caused to stumble because of Me on this night, because it is written, 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.'
verses.14:28: But after I have risen, I will go ahead of you into Galilee."
verses.14:29: But Peter said to Him, "Even if all are caused to stumble because of You, yet not I."
verses.14:30: And Jesus said to him, "Amen, I tell you that you, today, on this night, before a rooster crows twice, are going to deny Me three times."
verses.14:31: But he kept speaking even more, "Even if I must die together with You, I will not deny You." And all of them were also saying the same.
verses.14:32: And they came to an estate whose name was Gethsemane. And He said to His disciples, "Sit here while I pray."
verses.14:33: And He took Peter and James and John along with Him, and began to feel dread and deep distress.
verses.14:34: And He said to them, "My soul is sorrowful even to death; wait here and stay awake."
verses.14:35: And when He had gone forward a short distance, He fell down upon the ground and was praying that, if it were possible, the hour might pass from Him.
verses.14:36: And He said, "Abba, Father, all things are possible to You; take this cup away from Me; yet not what I wish, but what You wish."
verses.14:37: And He came and found them sleeping. And He said to Peter, "Simon, are you sleeping? Were you not able to stay awake for one hour?
verses.14:38: Stay awake and pray so that you may not enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is ready, yet the flesh is weak."
verses.14:39: And going away again, He prayed, saying the same words.
verses.14:40: And having returned, He once more found them sleeping, for their eyes were weighed down, and they did not know what they should answer Him.
verses.14:41: And He came a third time and said to them, "Sleep now and rest. It is enough; the hour has come. Look, the Son of Man will be handed over into the hands of sinners.
verses.14:42: Rise, let us go; look, the one who will hand Me over is near."
verses.14:43: And while He was still speaking, Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve, arrived, and with him a large crowd with swords and clubs from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.
verses.14:44: Now His betrayer had given them a sign, saying, "Whomever I kiss, He is the one; seize Him and lead Him away carefully."
verses.14:45: And when he had arrived, immediately approaching Him, he said, "Greetings, Rabbi," and kissed Him.
verses.14:46: Then they laid hands on Him and seized Him.
verses.14:47: But a certain one of those standing by, drawing a sword, struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his ear.
verses.14:48: And answering, Jesus said to them, "Have you come out as against a bandit with swords and clubs to apprehend Me?
verses.14:49: Every day I was with you in the temple teaching, and you did not seize Me; yet this is so that the Scriptures may be fulfilled."
verses.14:50: Then His disciples, abandoning Him, all fled.
verses.14:51: Now a certain young man was following Him, wrapped in a linen cloth over his bare body; and they seized him.
verses.14:52: But having cast off the linen cloth, he fled naked from them.
verses.14:53: And they led Jesus to the high priest, and all the priests and the scribes and the elders gathered together.
verses.14:54: Now Peter followed Him from a distance, all the way inside the courtyard of the high priest; and he was sitting with the attendants by the fire and warming himself.
verses.14:55: Now the chief priests and the whole council were seeking testimony against Jesus so that they might hand Him over to death, and they were finding none.
verses.14:56: For many were speaking false testimony against Him, yet the testimonies were not in agreement.
verses.14:57: And some, standing up, were bearing false testimony against Him, saying,
verses.14:58: "We heard Him saying, 'I will tear down this temple made by hand, and within three days I will build another not made by hand.'"
verses.14:59: And their testimony was not in agreement.
verses.14:60: And the high priest, rising up into the center, questioned Jesus, saying, "Do You answer nothing to the things that are charged against You by these men?"
verses.14:61: But He kept silent and answered nothing. Again the high priest was questioning Him and said to Him, "Are You the Christ, the Son of the blessed God?"
verses.14:62: But Jesus said to him, "I am; and you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the power of God and coming with the clouds of heaven."
verses.14:63: Then the high priest, tearing his garments, said, "Why do we still require witnesses?
verses.14:64: You have heard the blasphemy; how does it seem to you?" And all of them condemned Him as deserving of death.
verses.14:65: And some began to spit on Him, and to cover His face, and to strike Him with fists, and to say to Him, "Prophesy!" And the attendants were striking Him with slaps.
verses.14:66: And while Peter was below in the courtyard, one of the servant girls of the high priest came.
verses.14:67: And when she saw Peter warming himself, looking closely at him, she said, "You too were with Jesus the Nazarene."
verses.14:68: But he denied it, saying, "I neither know nor understand what you are saying." And he went outside in front of the courtyard, and a rooster crowed.
verses.14:69: And when the servant girl saw him again, she began to say to those standing by, "This man is one of them."
verses.14:70: But he denied it again. And after a little while, those who were standing nearby were again saying to Peter, "Truly you are one of them, for you are also a Galilean."
verses.14:71: But he began to invoke curses and to swear, "I do not know this man whom you are speaking of."
verses.14:72: And immediately a rooster crowed a second time. And Peter recalled the word that Jesus had spoken to him, "Before a rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times." And he began to weep.
verses.15:1: And immediately in the morning, the chief priests, taking counsel with the elders, the scribes, and the entire council, bound Jesus, led Him, and handed Him over to Pilate.
verses.15:2: And Pilate questioned Him, "Are You the King of the Jews?" But answering, He said to him, "You say so."
verses.15:3: And the chief priests kept accusing Him of many things.
verses.15:4: Then Pilate questioned Him again, saying, "Do You not answer anything? See how many things they are accusing You of."
verses.15:5: Yet Jesus answered nothing further, so that Pilate was astonished.
